content.user_title: Build Reliable Rust Tests for Guts
content.value_statement: Distributed systems fail in ways that simple unit tests can miss. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan unit, integration, property, fuzz, CI, and mock-based tests for Guts.
actual_capabilities: Explains a testing pyramid for high-reliability distributed systems.
Shows Rust unit test structure with grouped test modules and assertions.
Demonstrates async tests with tokio and bounded timeouts.
Describes integration fixtures for temporary nodes and repository workflows.
Covers proptest property tests, cargo-fuzz targets, CI matrices, and mockall-based mocks.
limitations: Focused on Rust and the Guts project structure, not general testing for every language.
Provides examples and strategy, but does not generate a full test suite by itself.
Command examples assume Cargo tooling and relevant test crates are already installed.
Does not validate project-specific APIs without access to the repository source.

use_cases.title: Add Coverage for Core Rust Modules
use_cases.description: Use the unit test patterns to organize module tests and verify expected errors for repository logic.

use_cases.title: Validate Distributed Synchronization
use_cases.description: Use temporary multi-node fixtures to test repository creation, cloning, connection, and synchronization flows.

use_cases.title: Harden Protocol Parsing
use_cases.description: Use property tests and fuzz targets to check round trips, signatures, and parser resilience against arbitrary input.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Unit Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for focused module coverage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Guts module and propose unit tests for success cases, error cases, and boundary values. Keep the plan grouped by function.

prompt_templates.title: Write Async Test Cases
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for async Rust behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add tokio-based async tests for this service. Include timeouts, clear assertions, and failure cases for long-running operations.

prompt_templates.title: Design Integration Fixtures
prompt_templates.prompt: Design integration test fixtures for temporary Guts nodes. Cover repository creation, peer connection, clone behavior, and cleanup requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Add Property and Fuzz Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify invariants in this protocol code and propose proptest cases plus a cargo-fuzz target. Explain what failures each test should catch.

output_examples.input: Ask for a test strategy for repository creation and cloning.
output_examples.output: A layered plan with unit cases for validation, integration cases for clone workflows, and multi-node checks for synchronization.

output_examples.input: Ask how to test message parsing robustness.
output_examples.output: A property-based test outline for valid round trips and a fuzzing target that verifies arbitrary bytes never crash the parser.

output_examples.input: Ask how to prepare CI for Guts tests.
output_examples.output: A CI matrix recommendation that runs workspace tests across Rust toolchains and operating systems, with optional coverage and fuzz jobs.

best_practices: Start with deterministic unit tests before adding slower integration and fuzz tests.
Use temporary directories and isolated fixtures for tests that create repositories or nodes.
Run command examples only in trusted project workspaces after reviewing local build scripts.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on end-to-end tests for distributed system behavior.
Do not leave async tests without timeouts or clear failure assertions.
Do not run fuzzing or benchmark commands automatically in untrusted repositories.

faq.question: What project is this skill designed for?
faq.answer: It is designed for Guts, a Rust distributed system, and its repository, node, protocol, and storage testing needs.

faq.question: Can it help with ordinary Rust unit tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes module organization, assertions, expected error handling, and async test patterns.

faq.question: Does it include integration testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes temporary node fixtures and multi-node repository synchronization tests.

faq.question: Does it support property-based testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses proptest examples for repository names, signature verification, and invariant checks.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents Cargo commands, but users should decide when and where to run them.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
